A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FairICP research. Their main text, equations, figures, algorithms, and Appendices A–D are available and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation results, CP/ICP sampling-quality experiments, and evaluations on Communities and Crime and COMPAS, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v3 reports original simulations and evaluations on Communities and Crime, COMPAS, and Adult, with additional comparisons and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: FairICP retains the inverse permutation distribution, adversarial losses, alternating training updates, hypothesis-testing procedure, and pairwise sampler. FairCP is introduced as an experimental comparator rather than a modification to FairICP.

E1.justification: v3 adds Adult income classification with sex and race protection, substantially broadening the empirical domains beyond the retained crime and recidivism tasks. Gaussian sampling-scenario coverage is less clear: v1 shows separate Gaussian and mixed-Gamma panels, while v3 specifies mixed-Gamma inputs but Figure 5 still mentions both.

E2.justification: v3 adds FairCP to the downstream predictive simulations, alongside FairICP, FDL, and Oracle. This supplies a direct comparator using non-inverted conditional permutation within the same adversarial framework; v1 compared CP and ICP only for sampling quality. The existing real-data comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The sampling-quality study expands K0 from {1,5} to {1,5,10}, extends nuisance dimensions through 100 instead of 20, and revises its stated response-generating law. v3 also removes COMPAS DEO evaluation and introduces runtime comparisons at approximately matched fairness levels. Existing training-size, split, and optimization grids largely remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new FairCP control tests whether inversion improves downstream fairness–accuracy tradeoffs, beyond v1's sampling-quality comparison. Density-quality sensitivity experiments also extend to substantially higher dimensions. Oracle comparisons, low-dependence simulations, and linear-model checks already existed and are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 explicitly reports prediction-loss standard deviations, including COMPAS results whose v1 figures showed point estimates. The existing 100 simulation runs/random splits and 20 sampling-quality trials are retained; the PDFs do not establish an increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: v3 adds Adult results, FairCP tradeoff curves, runtime measurements, and expanded or replaced sampling-quality results. For example, Table 1 newly reports Adult FairICP loss 0.157, KPC 0.007, and runtime 293.1 seconds. DEO results disappear. These additions and removals do not establish a same-setting improvement of FairICP between versions.

T1.justification: The central theorems and KPC definition remain. v3 adds a one-observation counterexample in Remark 2.2, refines conditioning in Appendix A's first proof, explicitly requires predictor/test-data independence in Proposition 2.5, and develops CP/ICP total-variation bounds in Appendix C, equations (14)–(15). These are localized mathematical additions and refinements.

C1.justification: v3 no longer lists adoption of a nonparametric fairness measure as a standalone contribution, presenting KPC as background instead. It also makes the first-framework positioning explicit. The central claims about inverse permutation, asymptotic equalized odds, and handling complex sensitive attributes remain.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly explains finite-sample permutation limitations even with known densities and CP's preservation of sensitive-attribute marginals. Its real-data interpretation emphasizes best performance across tasks and computational tradeoffs, whereas v1 described COMPAS performance as closely matching Reduction. Existing density-estimation and computational limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds runtime information and a versioned KPC package reference while retaining most architecture and hyperparameter details. It removes v1's code and Communities and Crime access links and the explicit statement excluding sensitive attributes from Crime predictors. These omissions do not establish code withdrawal or an actual input change.

R1.justification: The revised background adds conditional-independence references such as Azadkia and Chatterjee's CODEC and Sen et al., and includes Louppe et al. in adversarial-learning positioning. Several broader fairness/post-processing citations disappear. The principal relationship to Romano et al.'s FDL and Berrett et al.'s CP remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, method explanations, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. The former fairness-measurement section is divided between introductory background and the method section; sampling-quality experiments move partly from Appendix C into the main text, and real-data experiments are consolidated.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 1, merges simulation plots into multipanel figures, reorganizes sampling-quality displays, adds Table 1 and Adult plots, and redraws COMPAS scatter results as tradeoff curves. Real-data power panels move to Appendix D.3, alongside substantial changes to typography, margins, legends, and captions.

improvement.justification: The FairCP control better isolates inversion's contribution to downstream performance, while Adult evaluations and clearer finite-sample qualifications strengthen validation and interpretation. These provide a modest net improvement over v1. Gains are tempered by the removal of DEO evaluations and code-access information, and ambiguous FDL cells in Table 1.
